heading: SAE reconstruction errors can be more harmful than equally large random errors
definition: replacing activations with SAE reconstructions harms the model's loss more than random errors of the same size, so the error matters to what the model computes.
summary: Several independent studies find greater harm from SAE reconstruction errors than from equally large isotropic random errors. The broader claim is contested because structured random comparisons show near-baseline sensitivity.

suggested_status.by_scale: 1–10B: R2 for the epsilon-random KL comparison, with ScopeSAE loss reversals under different methods. <1B: ? for relative pathology; the explicitly sized Qwen result lacks a matched-random comparator. Size not stated: C for the GPT2-small comparator-distribution challenge. Toy, 10–100B and >100B: no coverage shown.
suggested_status.reason: The broad wording is contested because arXiv:2410.12555#r3–#r5 reports near-baseline sensitivity against structured random perturbations despite reproducing the isotropic comparison. lw:rZPiuFxESMxCDHe4B#r1–#r2 supplies KL and cross-entropy evidence against epsilon-random errors; arXiv:2507.00269#r2 reproduces excess KL on OpenLLaMA-3B using Gurnee's epsilon-random reconstruction test and the same KL-divergence measure. This direct V3 test belongs in tranche T1 rather than T2; its different NFM architectures provide method-performance comparisons rather than a different method for the direct V3 test. arXiv:2610.04905#r13 supplies the explicitly sized sub-1B loss reversal without random controls. counts: versions.V3.studies_with_challenges = 1; versions.V3.studies_with_limits_scope = 4; versions.V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0. Scale coverage follows versions.V3.studies_by_size and versions.V3.coverage_by_operation; it does not establish matched-random replication at every listed size.
suggested_status.open_questions: Would cross-entropy loss retain an SAE-specific excess against covariance-random and real-activation mixture errors across model families and layers? Would matched-random controls preserve or qualify ScopeSAE and vision-SAE loss improvements? Such results would clarify whether the broad claim remains contested or a distribution-specific version merits R2.

sources.headline: GPT2-small SAE reconstructions changed predictions more than isotropic random substitutions at matched distances.
OpenLLaMA-3B SAE reconstructions caused 2.99 times the KL divergence of equal-sized random errors.
GPT2-small residual-stream SAE substitutions increased loss more than equal-sized random errors across all layers.
GPT2-small SAE reconstruction effects varied considerably relative to mixture baselines across layers.
GPT2-small attention-output SAEs showed weaker excess harm; residual-stream harm varied across tokens.
ScopeSAE reconstructions lowered cross-entropy when gradients chose layers and replacements were defined relative to the target.
CLIP ViT-L SAE reconstructions lowered contrastive loss on ImageNet-1k.
GPT2-small SAE reconstructions nearly matched KL divergence from mixtures using activation covariances or real activations.

untested.what: A cross-entropy comparison of SAE reconstruction against covariance-random or real-activation mixture errors is not reported. This coverage gap is inferred from the reported methods and results: the structured-baseline challenge measures mean next-token KL divergence, while the matched-random cross-entropy result uses epsilon-random errors.

wording_issues.phrase: random errors of the same size
wording_issues.issue: Matching perturbation size does not specify its distribution. In GPT2-small experiments on approximately 2 million Openwebtext tokens, excess mean next-token KL is observed against isotropic random substitution. In the comparison across SAE models, excess is absent against covariance-random and real-activation mixture baselines, whose average KL is generally similar to SAE reconstruction. Closeness to mixture baselines varies considerably across layers.

The evidence combines cross-entropy loss increases with KL divergence from original predictions. The OpenLLaMA replication and structured-baseline challenge measure KL; they do not directly establish a cross-entropy loss comparison.

wording_issues.phrase: replacing activations with SAE reconstructions harms
wording_issues.issue: The statement needs conditions on SAE architecture and intervention. ScopeSAE writeback and the CLIP vision SAE lower their reported losses; GPT2-small attention SAEs include settings without excess KL over epsilon-random errors.

wording_issues.phrase: so the error matters to what the model computes
wording_issues.issue: The interventions establish sensitivity of predictions or loss to reconstruction error. The structured-baseline results qualify any stronger inference that this sensitivity is distinctive to SAE errors, rather than shared with other structured perturbations.

method_sensitivity.what: On GPT2-small, excess KL is observed against isotropic random substitution. In arXiv:2410.12555's comparisons across SAE models, excess is absent against covariance-random and real-activation mixtures, whose average KL is generally similar to SAE reconstruction KL; these experiments use approximately 2 million Openwebtext tokens. The comparator distribution changes the outcome while the isotropic-baseline result is reproduced.

GPT2-small residual-stream reconstruction gives a larger excess over epsilon-random KL than attention z-vector reconstruction. With mixture baselines, proximity to baseline also varies considerably across layers.

For GPT2-small residual-stream interventions, theta-random variants give approximately the epsilon-random KL, while rescaling the SAE reconstruction to the original activation norm leaves KL high and slightly increases it relative to the uncorrected reconstruction.

For single-token GPT2-small residual-stream interventions, the greater-than-2-times KL gap generally persists from position 32 to position 33. Layer 11 at position 33 is an exception whose magnitude and direction are not given. Individual-token comparisons at layer 6 also show substantial heterogeneity.

method_sensitivity.factor: ScopeSAE evaluation subset and selection target
method_sensitivity.what: For Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct at k=64, overall DeltaCE is −0.197 ± 0.009 with next-token selection and −0.206 ± 0.011 with predicted-token selection, reported as mean ± standard deviation. On tokens where the original top prediction matches the next token, the respective values are −0.438 and −0.469. With next-token selection on mismatching tokens, DeltaCE is +0.144. These are comparisons with original activations, without matched random errors.

method_sensitivity.factor: ScopeSAE sparsity budget and decoder objective
method_sensitivity.what: On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, DeltaCE first becomes negative at k=56; no value is provided at that threshold. Standard ScopeSAE gives DeltaCE −0.20, while decoder KL fine-tuning changes it to +0.07 with the encoder and biases frozen. The fine-tuned result has no matched-random comparator.

method_sensitivity.factor: SAE training method and perturbation length
method_sensitivity.what: At GPT2-small layer 6 resid_pre, local SAE error-direction curves track the covariance-random mixture. For e2e+ds SAEs, KL curves remain low before rising sharply around perturbation length 50. Below 50, the text states that lower L0 produces greater KL; above 70, it states that lower L0 produces a stronger effect. The L0 = 21.0 or 27.5 exceptions apply only to e2e SAEs. The end-to-end rows are marked cannot_determine for V3; they show different perturbation-response shapes without establishing the matched-error claim.
